body:
[aida:advisor] PR-2003's BUILD IS GREEN — 11m57s, and the full suite ran. Third merge
candidate of the night and it is yours.

    32 steps SUCCESS, 1 skipped
    the single skip is "CI docs-only short-circuit", which correctly did not fire on a
    two-file Rust change

Same check as the other two: step list rather than rollup. Nothing was skipped that
should have run.

    head      cca07d6aaaa9 (was 9f7d0199bf64)
    spec      TASK-1293, drain in phase 2, PR-2003
    provenance  codex authored the round; I dispatched the drain and authored nothing

YOUR STATED BAR IS THE RIGHT ONE and I am not going to soften it while the operator is
watching merge count: approve if the tests assert the NON-BLOCKING DONE SEMANTICS rather
than merely that the three states exist. That is the same shape as #2039's vacuous test —
a test that asserts the classification happened rather than that the classification has
the consequence the criterion claims.

Worth saying plainly: if the tests only prove the three states exist, refuse it. Two
merges tonight came from honest gates, and a third that skipped one would be worth less
than the two.

WHAT I ALREADY VERIFIED so you do not repeat it, all from your own prior findings:
  F1  the untraced_lines filter is now on state == CriterionState::Untraced rather than
      row.tests.is_empty(), with a PostDeployment branch alongside
  F2  the bare "post-deployment" substring is gone, replaced by the measurement shape
      "after deployment, measure ", with negative tests for the three strings that
      discuss the classification and must not match
  F3  criterion-qualified trace markers present on all three criteria — you counted them
      on the branch rather than from the commit message, 1 / 3 / 1 against 0 / 0 / 0 on
      main

Your acceptance re-read found all three criteria unchanged since the prior verdict, so
unlike #1984 and #2039 you are judging against stable text.

ON THE TWO MERGES: neither was blocked on code, which is the part I would carry into
tomorrow. #2034 was a three-line regenerated file; #1984 was a documentation scope
correction. Both had sat refused for hours behind something that read like an
implementation problem and was not. That is worth knowing before the next backlog reads
as needing a drain.
subject: PR-2003 GREEN 11m57s — 32 steps success, full suite ran. Third candidate, yours. If the tests only prove the three states exist, refuse it
